title: Rejoining the church in Brooklyn
summary: Green says he rejoined the church at the invitation of Mrs. Rights in Brooklyn on Putnam Street, to be rebaptized and get a new cornerstone.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: God moves in mysterious ways, you see. See, because I got to -- I had to rejoin the church. And I was already a Baptist, right. So, like not to get off the occasion of the count -- comment is that there's a church up there in Brooklyn in New York City, the Big Apple, you know. Fun Foreign City they calls it now.

And that really is fun, you know, because you can get rebaptized, and also you can get a new (unintelligible) you see. It's called a new cornerstone. And it's a lovely mother woman -- a lady -- she got her son -- grown son (unintelligible). I don't know whether he has made her a grandparent yet. But she was the one that invited me to go and rejoin the church, you know, up there in Brooklyn on Putnam Street.
And I just called the mother Mrs. Rights, you know. And she said, well, you should go, you know. Said God is the one to get your degrees from, you know. So --
